versions.summary: Olive-drab military field radio (~8 units tall with antenna). Rounded-corner chassis and dark front panel are extruded rounded-rectangle profiles. Left column: two analog gauges with lathe bezels, cream faces, nine tick marks and seeded amber needles. Right column: two lathe-turned rotary knobs with pointer caps and arc tick scales. Push buttons and a red indicator across the top, louvered speaker grille below, steel front socket with a short drop cable. Left side carries a stepped telescopic antenna (lathe, to ~8.2), a knurled steel cord socket, a steel latch with stud, and vent slots; top carries a green channel post with metal cap and a ribbed black knob. Right side mounts a telephone-style handset (tube handle, ellipsoid ear/mouthpieces) fed by a rubber cord arcing over the top. A long coiled cord exits the left socket, helixes ~4.6 turns down beside the case, then finishes in a flat shrinking spiral coil resting on the ground. Hidden geometry: plain back shell and underside implied by the chassis extrusion; four rubber feet contact the ground.

review.summary: The render is a recognizable vintage field radio/field telephone with the correct olive rounded chassis, dark inset control panel, two gauges, two large knobs, lower speaker grille, side-mounted handset, coiled cord, top controls, and tall whip antenna. Overall silhouette and proportions are coherent, though the handset and antenna are noticeably simplified.
issues: Make the right-side handset read as a single contoured receiver with distinct earpiece/mouthpiece ends rather than a thin U-shaped tube with bulbous caps.
Thicken and segment the antenna base and lower whip; the current antenna is overly needle-like and slightly too tall.
Add more layered depth around the front panel controls and speaker grille so they better match the reference's recessed, beveled construction.
